title: Redwood May 2026 - All Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands. Leadership reviewed Q1 results and May priorities, product roadmap highlights (Hosted API, Dedicated capacity updates, Private deployment progress), operations and hiring, security/compliance milestones, and open Q&A. Several follow-ups assigned for decks, hiring cadence, and SOC2 evidence requests.
topics: Product roadmap: API, Dedicated, Private, Optimize
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-13 10:00 PDT | Duration: 1:18 | Attendees: Priya Menon, Mateo Alvarez, Li Wei, Samira Patel, Ethan Ross + all employees

[00:00] Priya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're gonna get started. Quick note: recording is on, the deck's in the chat.
[00:18] Mateo: Quick ops note, rolling deploy this weekend for the new batching, should shave about 8 to 12% off token cost, assuming no surprises.
[00:30] Samira: I'll be brief, product highlights first, then Mateo will do infra, Li on research, and Ethan on go-to-market.
[00:45] Priya: Cool. High level — we had a strong Q1, usage up 42% month-over-month, team hit major milestones on Dedicated capacity and a number of mid-market deals moved to pilot. Net retention is healthy, and spending discipline held well.
[01:20] Samira: On the roadmap: Hosted API improvements — streaming reliability fixes, function calling maturity, and better structured output support. We're also shipping a new model catalog UI next week.
[01:50] Samira: Redwood Optimize work is in beta with three customers, focusing on batching and quantization profiles; early results show 20\u201330% cost reductions for inference heavy flows.
[02:15] Li: Research update — we've landed attention kernel optimizations, and KV cache heuristics; note, sometimes the transcript says KV cash, that's not right, it's KV cache, sorry. The runtime is seeing 15% latency p90 improvement on 8k seqs in our perf lab.
[02:50] Mateo: Ops — Dedicated capacity autoscaler tuning is in prod, we've tuned burst capacity thresholds. Also, added support for mixed-quantization pools which should help certain LLM variants.
[03:20] Mateo: We had an incident last month around a leader election flake; root cause was a znode race during a rolling restart. That is fixed, and we've added more sentinel checks.
[03:45] Ethan: Sales highlights — closed three mid-market pilots, notable one with FinCorp (confidential), security was a gating factor but we moved them to dedicated pilot with VPC and KMS.
[04:05] Priya: Security & compliance — we're making progress on the SOC 2 Type II timeline, internal audit run next month. ISO scope work is underway. Reminder: if you're on customer projects asking for audit evidence, route via compliance@.
[04:35] Employee-1: Quick question — what's the ETA on private on-prem packaging for regulated customers?
[04:42] Li: We're on track for an early-access private package in Q3; scheduling and installation docs coming after the beta. There are some network dependencies though, so expect a small setup window.
[05:05] Mateo: Region expansion — new EU region is live for a small subset of customers, latency profiles look good, next step is adding capacity and routing by policy.
[05:30] Samira: Product success — we packed more telemetry into the console, token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards, this should help customers optimize quickly.
[05:55] Priya: People updates — hiring: we opened roles for two infra SREs, one senior runtime engineer, and three sales ops. The hiring foo, uh, the hiring cadence is ramping, recruiters will reach out for referrals.
[06:20] Employee-2: How are we thinking about pricing pressure and open-source model availability?
[06:28] Ethan: We see pressure, yes — customers ask about running open models themselves. Our angle is predictable inference economics and operational tooling; we show cost/lats and where Dedicated helps. Also offer migration plans to private deployments where it makes sense.
[06:55] Priya: Funding and strategy — quick reminder, Series C closed in 2024, runway and growth plan intact. We're prioritizing enterprise features and regional expansion this year.
[07:20] Li: Tech deep-dive snippet — for folks curious we will post a technical blog on kernel selection and sequence-length aware compilation; TL;DR the runtime uses heuristics to pick kernels that minimize memory copies.
[07:50] Mateo: Observability — new tracing hooks are in the console; benchmarking spreadsheets are shared in the product channel. If you want to run internal benchmarks, grab the template from the repo.
[08:10] Priya: OK let's open to Q&A — please use raise hand or chat.
[08:20] Employee-3: On SOC 2 evidence, do customers get access to logs?
[08:28] Li: We provide audit logs for Private and Dedicated customers, hosted customers get redacted logs per our policy. We integrate with KMS for envelope encryption.
[08:40] Employee-4: Any updates on experimentations with quantization for LLAMA family?
[08:48] Li: We're testing 4-bit quantization profiles, early perf shows good tradeoffs but need more evals for hallucination/regression risk.
[09:05] Ethan: Marketing/customer momentum — two reference case studies being prepared, not public yet.
[09:20] Priya: Hiring question from chat — relocation budgets are negotiable per role.
[09:35] Mateo: Quick infra note — please file infra tickets to request capacity for experiments; don't overwhelm the provisioning queue.
[09:50] Employee-5: Any company offsite plans?
[09:58] Priya: We're exploring a Q3 offsite, likely a regional hub model to keep costs reasonable; survey going out next week.
[10:15] Q&A continues with mix of product nitty-gritty and org questions, small interruptions, folks drop-in/out.
[25:00] Priya: Back to roadmap — we're launching per-route fallback policies; that helps apps stay online when primary model or region is saturated.
[28:10] Samira: Canary deploys for model rollouts are in alpha, and there's an A/B testing framework for model variants.
[31:00] Mateo: Autoscaling knobs: latency-first policies vs cost-first policies, educate your customers on tradeoffs.
[34:20] Employee-6: Anything on pricing changes?
[34:30] Ethan: No immediate list-price change; we're experimenting with committed-reservation discounts for Dedicated.
[37:50] Security question in chat — do we support customer-managed keys for hosted?
[38:00] Li: For hosted we do envelope encryption with KMS; for Private/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed KMS/HSM where required.
[41:10] Priya: Performance numbers — p50 improved slightly due to new kernels; p95/p99 work ongoing. We are prioritizing reliability over experimental perf wins until the rollouts stabilize.
[44:40] Employee-7: Where do we stand on support SLAs for smaller customers?
[44:50] Ethan: We have tiered SLAs; small self-serve customers get best-effort, enterprise gets SLA ladder with faster response and on-call.
[47:05] Mateo: Note on cost engineering — Optimize team is making recommendations on batching windows; see the Optimize channel for details.
[49:30] Priya: Okay final section: leadership asks and action items recap.
[50:00] Priya: Samira, please share the updated roadmap deck and product notes.
[50:05] Samira: Will do.
[50:12] Priya: Mateo, follow up on the leader-election postmortem and share ops runbook.
[50:20] Mateo: On it.
[50:25] Priya: Li, please publish the kernel selection blog and put an internal TL;DR for non-engineers.
[50:32] Li: Yep.
[50:35] Priya: Ethan, share the pilot lists and a two-slide summary for each notable customer.
[50:42] Ethan: Yep, I'll send.
[50:45] Priya: I'll share the deck, video, and the offsite survey. Thanks everyone, let's keep momentum.
[51:00] Meeting ends, folks linger in chat and threads for follow-ups.

Notes on transcript quality: automated captions picked up some technical terms incorrectly (e.g., KV cash vs KV cache, z-node as znode), speaker labels may be approximate and a few overlaps/crosstalk occur.
